wa_south_ridge.overview: The classic route on South Peak following a scenic south-facing ridge. Features clean granite climbing with exposure and memorable features including a notable gap called the 'cannon hole'.

wa_mount_johnson_standard.descent_text: Reverse the ascent line: downclimb from the summit back to the ~6,900 ft Johnson–Clark notch, then retrace the talus-and-moraine descent down into Surprise Basin and back over its rim to Upper Royal Basin, from which the Royal Basin/Upper Dungeness Trail leads back out to the trailhead. The class 4 terrain near the summit is the crux of the descent as well as the ascent — the rock is loose enough in spots that most reported difficulty on this peak comes from downclimbing it, so face in and test holds on anything above class 3. Parties sometimes place a single short rappel (roughly 30–50 ft) to get past the steepest step just below the summit block rather than downclimbing it, particularly if the rock is wet or the party is less comfortable with the exposure; a single 30m rope is more than adequate for this, and any anchor would be a natural one (horn, chockstone, or slung block) — there are no fixed/bolted rappel stations reported on Johnson. Treat this rappel as optional/conditional rather than mandatory: capable parties in dry conditions generally downclimb the whole route.

pitch_detail.notes: Shallow right fork, slabby class 3 climbing on clean rock.
Brief class 4 step moving right into a second couloir.
Sustained slabby class 3 to the ridge crest.
Summit ridge traverse south, around towers on the west side, with brief class 4 moves.
